requirements.requirement: Cron entry on node1 runs /usr/local/bin/inventory-maintenance daily at 02:15
requirements.summary: Root crontab was set to '15 2 * * * /usr/local/bin/inventory-maintenance >> /var/log/inventory-maintenance.log 2>&1', confirmed present in /var/spool/cron/root, and confirmed intact with identical schedule/command after a full node restart.

Manually executing the exact cron command line produced and appended output to /var/log/inventory-maintenance.log, and the file's content was confirmed still present (unchanged) after the node restart. The actual 02:15 cron-triggered run was not observed live (future scheduled time), so this relies on a byte-identical manual proxy rather than an in-situ cron firing.

requirements.requirement: crond service is enabled and running so the schedule will actually fire
requirements.summary: crond was enabled and started (enable --now), verified active/enabled both before and after the restart.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol: pre-restart baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovered state on node1
requirements.summary: Pre-restart baseline captured boot_id c2f29441... with crond active, crontab present, log present, script executable. A native reboot was issued and acknowledged (stream closed), followed by a connection timeout and successful reconnection. Post-restart boot_id changed to e933b079..., matching the fixed lifecycle snapshots (global:before_prepare and global:after_executor boot-identity), and crond, crontab entry, script executable bit, and log content were all confirmed intact afterward.

overall_summary: The executor correctly scheduled /usr/local/bin/inventory-maintenance to run daily at 02:15 via root's crontab, ensured crond is enabled/active so the schedule executes, and demonstrated log retention in /var/log/inventory-maintenance.log via a byte-identical manual run of the cron command line. All of this, plus crond/crontab/log state, was independently re-confirmed intact after a full node restart with a directly observed boot-identity change, satisfying the restart-evidence protocol. The delivered script itself contains a pre-existing defect (an embedded literal 'SCRIPT' heredoc terminator causing a 'command not found' line in output each run), but this originates from the prepare-stage script content, not executor action, and does not affect satisfaction of the scheduling/retention contract.
limitations: The actual 02:15 cron-triggered execution was not observed live since that time had not yet occurred; retention was verified via a manual run of the identical command line instead.

The prepared /usr/local/bin/inventory-maintenance script contains an internal defect (a stray 'SCRIPT' token producing a 'command not found' error each run); this is preexisting script content, not an executor-introduced issue, but it means the retained log will always include this extra error line.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands map clearly to the task: chmod +x on the pre-existing 644 script (cmd-4844d3c6f1274ac1) was necessary since the prepared file was not executable; crontab install (cmd-20e52ea30ba94b8a) and crond enable (cmd-ea67841bf0d94074) directly satisfy the contract; the rm -f plus manual run of the log (cmd-72663089496f442c) is a bounded, low-risk test that produced the exact final log state required and left no residue; the reboot (cmd-6352ed58aa0e4edf) is the required restart-evidence action and was fully verified recovered afterward. No unnecessary mutations, abandoned files, failed services, or new exposure were observed (listening sockets and package-health identical in kind before/after, only PID/boot_id values changed as expected from the reboot).
